sections.title: Living Stones and a Holy Priesthood
observations: Peter begins by encouraging believers to rid themselves of malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander, which are detrimental to spiritual growth.
He describes believers as 'living stones' being built into a spiritual house, emphasizing the communal aspect of faith and the importance of the church as a living entity.
The imagery of a holy priesthood signifies that all believers have direct access to God and are called to offer spiritual sacrifices.

sections.title: The Cornerstone and Our Identity
observations: Peter quotes from the Old Testament, referring to Christ as the cornerstone, which is foundational for the faith.
He explains that while Christ is precious to believers, He is also a stone of stumbling for those who reject Him, highlighting the division in responses to the Gospel.
Believers are described as a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, and a people for His own possession, which speaks to their identity and purpose in the world.

sections.title: Conduct Among the Gentiles
observations: Peter urges believers to conduct themselves honorably among non-believers, as their behavior can lead others to glorify God.
He emphasizes submission to governing authorities, which reflects a commitment to order and respect for God's established order in society.
This section highlights the importance of living out one's faith in practical ways that reflect Christ's character.

sections.title: Suffering for Doing Good
observations: Peter addresses the reality of suffering for righteousness' sake, encouraging believers to endure and maintain their faith.
He points to Christ as the ultimate example of suffering, who did not retaliate but entrusted Himself to God.
This section reassures believers that their suffering is not in vain and is part of their calling as followers of Christ.

importantVerses.commentary: This verse encapsulates the identity of believers in Christ, emphasizing their chosen status and purpose.
This verse highlights the importance of good conduct among non-believers, which can lead to glorifying God.

questions: What does it mean to be a 'living stone' in the context of the church?
How can believers effectively conduct themselves honorably among non-believers?
In what ways can we understand suffering as part of our Christian calling?
